title: feat(types)!: the list view's kanban / calendar / gallery / timeline blocks follow their @objectstack/spec slots by reference (objectui#6152, round 11)
body:
Part of #6152 (round 11)
Clause-②: no

This is the round's implementing PR. The seat answered the round's measurement report (`6066412215`) with Q1 → A and Q2 → A on objectui#6152 (comment `6066456661`), under claim `6066077975`. Whether the card closes after this round is the seat's call, so this body carries no closing keyword. Session: `https://claude.ai/code/session_01DBZ9bntPZ7VKyQNtJeNsgw`.

## What changes

`ListViewSchema`'s four per-view-type blocks (`kanban`, `calendar`, `gallery`, `timeline`) in `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts` are now each the `@objectstack/spec` 17.7.0 `ListViewSchema` slot of that name, by reference (`stripImportedDefaults(SpecListViewSchema).shape.KIND.unwrap()`). That is the ROW's own member, the same construction round 9 used for the `object-calendar` container. Each block is strict: no `.passthrough()` and no hand-copied members. The only local keys are named refusals:

| block | refused key | the message names |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `kanban` | `groupField` | `groupByField` |
| `kanban` | `cardFields` | `columns` |
| `gallery` | `imageField` | `coverField` |
| `timeline` | `dateField` | `startDateField` |
| `calendar` | `defaultView` | no member: the spec has none on a list view's calendar block |

The earlier arms (`kanban.groupBy`, objectui#8365; `calendar.dateField` / `endField`, objectui#8355) are unchanged. Each new arm reports `invalid_type` at the key's own path. Its message opens with the spec's own lead sentence for that surface ("Unrecognized key(s) on this kanban configuration: ..."), then gives the canonical key.

- **`.partial()`** stays on `kanban` and `timeline` only, because app-shell installs derived defaults on a `list-view` node's declared slots that leave out a member the spec requires. `defaultKanbanFromObject` gives `{ groupByField }` with no `columns` (InterfaceListPage, ObjectDataPage), and InterfaceListPage's timeline default reuses `defaultCalendarFromObject`, so it has no `titleField`. `calendar` now requires `startDateField`, as the spec does: the census found no producer that leaves it out. The gallery slot requires nothing.
- **The TypeScript face** (`ListViewSchema['kanban']` and the other three, derived through `ListViewInferred`) loses its index signature. A typed literal with an undeclared key, an alias, `calendar.defaultView`, or a calendar block without a start is now a compile error.
- **The comment above the blocks is rewritten.** It drops the two premises the census disproved: the "real authored values" (they were a test fixture, `normalize-list-view.test.ts`), and CreateViewDialog as the reason for `.partial()` (both of its persisting doors add `columns` since objectui#11581). It names the real omitters instead. `list-view-spec-parity.test.ts` now points at that one comment instead of repeating the rationale.

## What did not move

The readers are untouched, as the ruling directs:

- `normalizeListViewSchema`'s alias fold;
- `ListView`'s `calendar.defaultView` lift;
- the kanban and calendar spreads;
- the projection collectors (Q2).

The render path parses nothing, so a view stored with one of these keys renders exactly as before; only authored metadata meets the refusal. The legacy `options.KIND` bag and the hand-written `ListViewGalleryConfig` / `ListViewTimelineConfig` index signatures are also unchanged. Both stay booked on objectui#6152.

## Fixtures the narrowing flips, re-spelled with their tests

- `calendar-date-alias-refusal-8355.test.ts`:
  - Its "PASSTHROUGH CONTROL" now pins the closed block: the spec's `unrecognized_keys` at `calendar`.
  - Its timeline scope row now pins `timeline.dateField` as refused by name. That row asked whoever retired the alias to say so.
- `default-view-agenda-retired.test.ts`: the list-view describe pins `calendar.defaultView` as refused for every value, with a lit control. The element's flat `defaultView` describes are unchanged.
- `list-view-spec-parity.test.ts`: the "still accepts the deprecated aliases" row becomes the by-name refusal row.
- `object-calendar-container-by-reference-6152.test.ts` (round 9): its open-object control now reads the `object-calendar` node itself, because the list-view block it used to read is closed.
- `object-kanban-group-by-limit-7322.test.ts`: the source-text pin reads the view-level `groupField` as a refusal arm. Its readers half is unchanged and still green.
- `kanban-stray-group-by-refusal-8365.test.ts`: the "legacy alias still compiles" control becomes a `@ts-expect-error` refusal.
- `plugin-list`, two test files:
  - `ListView.test.tsx`'s "should use spec kanban config" wrote the alias; it now writes `groupByField`. This was a typed fixture that broke only at type-check.
  - `ListView.strayGroupByRefused-8365.test.tsx`'s undeclared-key control pins the closed block.
- Docs, per AGENTS.md #2:
  - `packages/types/src/zod/README.md`: its table of local keys becomes the refusal table.
  - `content/docs/plugins/plugin-calendar.mdx`: round 9's sentence calling the list-view block "still `.passthrough()`" is replaced.
  - No guide or README shows a refused key on these four declared blocks. The census read none, and the plugin-list README's examples sit in the `options` bag, which is booked.

## New pin

`packages/types/src/__tests__/list-view-blocks-by-reference-6152.test.ts` holds 99 tests:

- the installed slots as a precondition: strict, with their required members;
- the mirror IS the slot: strict, every slot member present, and only refusal arms beside them;
- verdict equality with the slot over accepted and refused inputs, with a lit control that the table holds both kinds. The one sanctioned difference, `.partial()`, has a row per producer;
- one named-refusal pin per key: the slot's `unrecognized_keys`, then the mirror's `invalid_type` at the key's path with the canonical key in the message, through the mirror, `AnyComponentSchema`, `StrictAnyComponentSchema` and `safeValidateSchema`, with a lit control on each door;
- calendar's required `startDateField` on every door;
- undeclared keys refused on every door;
- the closed TS face: no index signature, eight `@ts-expect-error` directives, and a lit control.

## Tests

Head `acdfc2848`. Every heavy run went through `../objectstack/scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`.

- **The union**, on `a6a01c851`. That was HEAD then; the final head `acdfc2848` differs only by the re-spelled `ListView.strayGroupByRefused-8365.test.tsx`.
  - The command: `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/types/ packages/core/ packages/plugin-list/ packages/plugin-kanban/ packages/plugin-calendar/ packages/plugin-timeline/ packages/plugin-view/ apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts apps/console/src/__tests__/timelineAxisRefusalReach-7070.test.tsx`, plus app-shell's view producer and designer tests (`CreateViewDialog`, `ViewConfigPanel`, `ObjectView`, `InterfaceListPage`, `ObjectDataPage`, `view-config-adapter`, `ViewVariantInspector`).
  - The result: `Test Files 1 failed | 1001 passed (1002)`, `Tests 1 failed | 18200 passed | 159 skipped`. The one failure was that `plugin-list` control, re-spelled in `acdfc2848`.
  - `packages/plugin-gallery/` is not in the union, because no such package exists; ObjectGallery lives in `plugin-list`.
- **On the final content:** that file plus `scripts/__tests__/` gives `Test Files 180 passed | 2 skipped (182)`, `Tests 5463 passed | 2 skipped`, VERDICT command-exit 0. The new pin alone gives `Tests 99 passed (99)`.
- **type-check** (each row echoes `type-check`):
  - `@object-ui/types` is green. Its script runs `tsconfig.test.json`, so the new `@ts-expect-error` directives are live: an unused one would be TS2578.
  - After `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/console^...'` (34/34 successful), these are all Done: core, data-objectstack, react, plugin-calendar, plugin-dashboard, plugin-gantt, plugin-grid, plugin-kanban, plugin-map, plugin-timeline, plugin-tree, plugin-view, app-shell and console.
  - `plugin-list` went red once: TS2322 at the `groupField` line of "should use spec kanban config". Its test project resolves `@object-ui/types` through the rebuilt `dist`, so that red is also this change's cross-package reverse check. After the re-spelling it exits 0.
- **Gates on `acdfc2848`**, each exit 0:
  - `check:spec-symbols`, `check:component-surface-parity` and `check:doc-types`;
  - `check:doc-snippets` ("784 of 784 block(s) judged, 0 failed"), `check:doc-examples` and `check:skill-examples`;
  - `check:readme-exports` ("OK"). Its first run and the first doc-snippets run were PRECONDITION NOT MET, because `cli` and `plugin-ai` were unbuilt; the gate's own scoped build (35/35) cleared it;
  - `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:new-line-citations` ("0 new citation(s)") and `check:control-bytes`;
  - `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` (12 source files of 2 released packages; 1 changeset declared), `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, and `node scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --audit`.

## Acceptance notes

- `content/docs/plugins/plugin-calendar.mdx` and `packages/types/src/zod/README.md` are prose this round makes false. `plugin-list`'s two test files are fixtures the narrowing flips. All three are covered by the go-ahead's items 5, 6 and 8.
- Round 9's pending changeset ends "What did not move: the list view's own `calendar` block, which keeps `.passthrough()`". That was true of round 9. This round's changeset says it closes that block, and round 9's file is left untouched.
- Not governed: `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` answers NOT GOVERNED for all 14 paths.
